_doc: BBB v2 chunk A — covenants + operating metrics with source citations for the 8 BBB-tier hospital muni obligors identified in bbb_tier_universe_v2.json. Hospital MTIs typically state a DSCR rate covenant; days-cash-on-hand floors often live in bank/swap/credit agreements. Where verified, we record both the value and source. Where not verified, we mark LOW confidence with industry-typical defaults (65 days DCOH / 1.10x DSCR for BBB-tier hospital MTI).
_methodology: WebSearch + WebFetch against (1) rating-agency reports indexed via Moody's / S&P / Fitch press release titles, (2) Bond Buyer / Becker's / Daily Memphian / InDepthNH / Healthcare Dive trade press coverage of rating actions, (3) obligor IR / continuing disclosure pages where parseable, (4) MSRB EMMA where reachable, (5) state regulatory financial filings (FL Auditor for Hillsborough County Hospital Authority, Ohio Auditor for MetroHealth, CHIA for Lawrence General). PDFs from MSRB EMMA and continuing disclosure often returned binary content not parseable by WebFetch; we relied on rating-agency snippet text and trade press where that occurred.

_confidence_definitions.HIGH: Direct from MTI / Official Statement / continuing disclosure with verbatim numeric covenant value, OR rating agency press release body text quoting the value
_confidence_definitions.MEDIUM: Rating-agency report or trade press summary quoting the specific covenant value for THIS obligor
_confidence_definitions.LOW: Industry-typical default applied (no verified source for this obligor's specific covenant)

additional_covenants.name: Florida Development Finance Corporation conduit Series 2024A/B + Hillsborough IDA Series 2020
additional_covenants.description: TGH was downgraded by Moody's from A3 to Baa1 in 2020 in connection with $569M of new debt for capital projects increasing inpatient, outpatient, and surgical volumes. December 2023 closed $294M acquisition of Bravera Health (3 hospitals from CHS subsidiaries: 120-bed Bravera Health Brooksville, 128-bed Seven Rivers, 124-bed Spring Hill). Expanded system now six hospitals + 150+ care locations across Hillsborough, Citrus, Hernando, Pasco, Pinellas and Palm Beach counties.

operating_metrics.fiscal_year: FY2024 (ended 6/30/2024 per Fitch; Hillsborough County FY ends 9/30)
operating_metrics._notes: EBITDA margin 8.3% FY2024 (Fitch). $1.48B unrestricted cash and investments at FYE 2024. $1.269B long-term debt as of June 30 (~70% bond debt). Revenue $2.7B is conservative system-level estimate post-Bravera integration; actual likely higher. ADS estimated at ~$95M (7.5% of LT debt). Medicaid + self-pay under 25% of revenues. Operating margin not directly extracted; EBITDA margin 8.3% implies operating margin in low-to-mid single digits.

Tampa General Hospital._notes: Tampa General Hospital — Florida Health Sciences Center, Inc. d/b/a Tampa General. Conduit issuers: Florida Development Finance Corporation + Hillsborough County IDA. Split rating Baa1 (Moody's) / A- (S&P) / A (Fitch) — Moody's is binding. Major expansion via Bravera Health acquisition Dec 2023. Trajectory positive: outlook revised to positive by Moody's in 2024 and Fitch in October 2025.

The 125/75 notation indicates 125 actual days vs 75-day covenant minimum (per typical CFO-deck convention).

additional_covenants.name: Moody's Baa2 (in window) / Baa3 negative (Oct 30, 2025 — post-window)
additional_covenants.description: Moody's downgraded MetroHealth to Baa3 from Baa2 in Oct 30, 2025 report. Cited slower-than-expected operating improvement leading to liquidity decline. Charity care costs more than doubled since 2022 reaching 'unsustainable' levels; 66% governmental payer exposure; financial leadership turnover. Operating margin and exact LT debt not extracted from board meeting PDF (partially binary). The October 30, 2025 Moody's downgrade language implies liquidity declined materially during FY2025.

MetroHealth System._notes: MetroHealth System — Cleveland safety-net academic medical center; component unit of Cuyahoga County (OH). Issues directly. Moody's-only rated. Baa2 stable through window; downgraded to Baa3 negative Oct 30, 2025 (post-window). Textbook BBB-tier covenant tripwire candidate: lowest IG + negative outlook + 66% governmental payer + federal Medicaid cut risk + CEO turnover.

additional_covenants.name: December 2024 Moody's downgrade A2->A3 + S&P A+->A (both negative)
additional_covenants.description: Both Moody's and S&P downgraded one notch in December 2024 citing 'accelerated operating losses and diminished reserves'. Subsequent 2025 Moody's action took rating to Baa1/Negative. Drivers: lower supplemental funding estimates; Epic EHR conversion (Oct 2024 go-live) created accounts-receivable cycle disruption; Workday concurrent implementation. Pre-conversion, Methodist Le Bonheur reported a 1H 2023 operating loss of $110.3M on $910.5M revenue (-12.1% margin).

operating_metrics._notes: $910.5M 1H 2023 revenue with $110.3M operating loss (-12.1% margin) per Becker's; annualized revenue ~$2.0-2.2B with continued losses. Full-year FY2024 figures not surfaced (operating margin -8.5% is rough estimate based on H1 -12.1% trending toward improvement post-Epic). System reports 'early gains in revenue cycle performance and efficiency' following October 2024 Epic go-live and Workday/Ensemble Health Partners partnership.

Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare._notes: Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare — Memphis system, Baa1/BBB+ tier. Multiple-notch downgrade path: Moody's A2 -> A3 (Dec 2024) -> Baa1 (2025), S&P A+ -> A (Dec 2024) -> BBB+. Drivers: Tennessee supplemental funding cuts + IT/EHR/AR conversion disruption + ongoing operating losses. Becker's framed this as 'second downgrade in just over a year'.

Genesis Healthcare System (OH)._notes: Genesis Healthcare System (OH) — Zanesville. additional_covenants.name: S&P trajectory BB+ (2019 pre) -> BB (Feb 2019) -> B- (2024-10)
additional_covenants.description: Multi-notch deterioration over 2019-2024. Operating losses FY2015-2018; COVID compounded; Holy Family acquisition Oct 2024 added integration risk. May 2025 announced scale-back of Holy Family Haverhill (eliminating med-surg + ICU beds, transitioning to satellite ED + inpatient behavioral health).

operating_metrics._notes: CHIA Lawrence General Hospital profile PDF exists but binary (not parseable). $350M revenue estimate based on community hospital scale and ProPublica aggregator references. $65M MassDevelopment Series 2014 LT debt; ADS ~$5M. October 2024 Holy Family acquisition would have increased revenue base materially but also operating losses; the Boston Globe described Lawrence General as losing '$258,000 a day at the height of the Omicron surge' in 2022. May 2025 Haverhill campus downsizing implies continued operating distress.

Lawrence General Hospital._notes: Lawrence General Hospital — Massachusetts. Deeply distressed sub-IG community hospital. S&P B-/Stable per universe v2 (only rating). October 2024 acquired Holy Family hospitals from Steward bankruptcy estate for $28M. Rebranded as Merrimack Health 2025. May 2025: scaling back Holy Family Haverhill to satellite ED. NOT BBB-tier — this is a fallen-angel B-tier credit; universe v2 'medium confidence per universe v2' label appropriately flags this as edge case.
